exact_title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
source_type: arXiv preprint / AI-ML systems and reinforcement-learning study

main_text_figures.summary: Overview of the dual-role self-play loop and relative benchmark improvements across games and tool use.
Four generated environments across one 30B-A3B run, showing the curriculum becoming more stateful and multi-turn over training.
Core framework: corpus and memory feed the Environment Designer, hint/no-hint rollouts define designer regret, task return trains the Reasoning Agent, and both update shared weights.
Two positive-regret examples demonstrating how privileged hints alter Reasoning Agent search behavior and return.
Held-out games benchmark trajectories for the 30B-A3B run, showing gains in science, code, and procedural reasoning while competition math is largely preserved.
Learnable-share dynamics: full SPADE raises the fraction of generated environments with intermediate solve rates to roughly one-third late in training.
Environment diversity comparison showing corpus-grounded runs remain diverse while the no-corpus ablation collapses.
Environment evolution: formula disclosure declines across training; the no-corpus ablation repeats the same rotating-maze task.
Reasoning Agent behavior shifts from front-loaded derivation and format failure toward evidence-first interaction and later derivation.
Training curves for full and partial/frozen-designer ablations; partial variants peak early and degrade while full SPADE remains strongest late.
Environment Designer reward ablation comparing hint-based regret, EMA learning potential, and a frozen control.
Scale analysis: SPADE gain rises from +5.2 at 4B to +8.1 at 30B-A3B, while matched fixed-env GRPO stays near +1.2; smaller models show noisier regret.
Curriculum-breadth comparison: six-skill training outperforms the restricted two-skill curriculum on the eight-benchmark mean.

main_text_tables.summary: Matched games-setting results across Qwen3 4B, 8B, and 30B-A3B, including fixed-env GRPO, fixed-env RLVE, and SPADE on eight held-out benchmarks.
Tool-use benchmark results for SPADE across three Qwen3 scales plus contextual published rows from other environment-synthesis systems; cross-paper comparability is limited.
Component and frozen-designer ablations for the 30B-A3B games setting.

algorithms.summary: End-to-end generation, validation, hint/no-hint rollout, reward construction, and joint GRPO update loop.
